localBiteReport: The week of September 4–10 brought the first noticeable signs of the fall transition to Choctawhatchee Bay, with water temperatures at 87°F and enormous concentrations of bait beginning to push through the system. Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters reported baitfish schools moving from deeper open water into bayous, flats, bridge areas, and roll-downs — activity that should steadily improve redfish and general flats fishing as September progresses toward October. The influx of bait is setting the stage for better sight-fishing opportunities on the flats for reds, with local guides expecting the bite to build meaningfully over the coming weeks.
